newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - Capers firm, older Panamaxes ease.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - Capers firm, older Panamaxes ease.

text.p: Caper rates stayed generally firmer and in certain cases the most modern Panamaxes also remained in steady demand.

But weaknesses appeared for other Panamaxes, especially those over 10 years of age, in the Atlantic and North Pacific. The difference in rates obtainable by the newer and older Panamaxes has widened in these areas.
The BFI fell 5 points to 1506 on perceived softening conditions for Atlantic Panamaxes which outweighed the improving performance of the Capers.

Some brokers believed that there was now insufficient enquiry to sustain the Pacific Panamax market and pointed out that a number of vessels were currently eastbound in ballast from the Far East, possibly destined for the US Gulf. Meanwhile the Handy market showed few signs of improvement for owners with especially poor levels still prevailing in the US Gulf and Plate grain trades.

With little activity in the aTlantic in the Panamax category on voyage basis (Bounty was said to have failed with Cobelfret for 65,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Ghent for end Jan at $13.00) attention was concentrated on timecharter business. S Koreans were reported to have booked Thetis 73,600 dwt delivery US Gulf end Jan trip Far East at a significantly lower $15,000 daily plus $290,000 bonus. Ascona 64,942 dwt prompt in Denmark was rumoured fixed by NNC for a transatlantic round to Egypt at an unknown rate, and Tomis Fah 65,262 dwt which fixed Geepee delivery Morocco retro Jan 10 trip via US Gulf to Kosichang at $14,450 daily failed on subjects.

Theomitor 77,298 dwt was understood fixed to Marifran delivery Continent early Feb for 7-9 months at $10,750 daily. There were reports of Halla taking Mui Kim 68,774 dwt delivery UK mid Feb for 12 months at $12,000 daily, and the Torm-relet Mehmet bey 68,789 dwt being covered delivery Continent end Jan for a similar period on private terms.

Period business was also fixed by grain interests in the Pacific: Banya 73,000 dwt was linked with Continental delivery prompt S Korea for 5-7 or 7-9 months at $11,500 daily, and Casinomar fixed Anangel Omonia 73,519 dwt on subjects delivery Japan end Jan for 3-5 months at $11,650 daily.

Rates and conditions were much less favourable for the older Panamaxes. The 1976-built Archangelos 64,352 dwt was rumoured booked by HMM on subjects NoPac/S Korea at $8,750/9,000 daily plus bb, but Simeon CH 60,734 dwt fixed in the low $8,000's delivery Japan via NoPac to Iran by Irano-hind and Petra 64,848 dwt delivery NoPac early Feb to Bin Qasim by Shadab at $10,000 daily plus $160,000 bonus were both said to have failed on subjects. NSAC quoted a fresh enqury of 54,000 heavy grain NoPac/Taiwan for Jan/Feb and Glencore 25,000 barley S Australia or NSW/China prompt. In the Atlantic new orders included Continental with 40/48,000 50' Mississippi/Jeddah Jan/Feb (ideas $21.00). Reports circulated that Cargill fixed Maritime Pearl for 37,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Continent at only $13.50, and that Glencore might have covered 25,000 meals US Gulf/Spanish Med for prompt loading.

Stronger rates were seen in a number of trades - Elsam, for example, paid as much as $7.50 to Excelsior for 100,000 coal Hampton Roads/Ensted and $8.75 to Chrismir for 140,000 Richards Bay/Ensted, both for early Feb shipment. Rohstoffhandel conceded $6.17-1/2 to Olivia for 150,000 ironore Tubarao/Rotterdam for mid Feb but New Harvest was still on subjects with Bocimar for 200,000 ironore Tubarao/Japan for Feb 15/28 at $10.50. SCF Trust 96,000 dwt failed on subjects with P and O for coal Hampton Roads/Rotterdam for end Jan at $6.50, said to be because the size was inadequate. The 1995-built Atlantica 63,990 dwt failed on subjects with UBT for fertilizers Black Sea/China, but brokers reported strong demand for Panamax tonnage for fertilizers from the Baltic to China.

Four vessels of 30/40,000 dwt have fixed Continent/US Gulf business, 2 each for account of Combac and Western Bulkcarriers at rates between $6,000 and $7,000 daily, but full details are lacking. Little was reported in the East although conditions were described as steady. Korea Line were linked with Iolcos Garnet 31,793 dwt delivery NoPac trip Far East at close $7,000/7,250 daily plus $135,000 bonus.
